```{r results-define-plot-theme}
#Shared plot style (taken from the circle plot of transformations)
# Font:    Helvetica
# Palette: scico "lipari" (light -> dark). Plots with only 2-3 colours use warm + bluish
#          tones only (see pal_lipari()); plots with 4+ colours use the full palette.
# Theme:   theme_minimal(base_size = 14), no ticks, grey92 grid, bold legend title (13),
#          legend text (12), bold centered title (18), grey40 subtitle (13)
# Labels:  sentence case ("Number of studies", "Range correction type", ...)

lit_font <- "Helvetica"

# Full palette (11 steps, light -> dark)
lipari_11 <- c("#FDF4D9", "#EACCA4", "#E5AA7F", "#E88768", "#CE685E", "#A36267",
               "#7F5F70", "#615D78", "#3B5378", "#0F3456", "#021326")

# Reduced palette for plots that need only 1-3 colours:
# warm and bluish tones only (skips the muted purple/mauve mid-tones
# "#A36267", "#7F5F70", "#615D78" and the near-white / near-black ends)
lipari_few <- list(
  "1" = "#E88768",
  "2" = c("#E88768", "#3B5378"),
  "3" = c("#E5AA7F", "#CE685E", "#3B5378")
)

# Palette picker: n <= 3 -> warm + bluish subset, n >= 4 -> full lipari (reversed scico)
pal_lipari <- function(n) {
  if (n < 1) return(character(0))
  if (n <= 3) lipari_few[[as.character(n)]] else rev(scico(n = n, palette = "lipari"))
}

# Number of distinct non-NA levels (used to pick the palette size)
n_lev <- function(x) length(unique(stats::na.omit(x)))

# Single accent colour (plots with only one colour)
col_single <- lipari_few[["1"]]

# Make all text / label geoms use the same font
update_geom_defaults("text",  list(family = lit_font))
update_geom_defaults("label", list(family = lit_font))

# Define a theme for pretty plots
lit_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = lit_font) +
  theme(
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40")
  )
```

```{r circle-plot-transformations}
# For modern scientific color palettes
#data.frame(colname = data_extract %>% colnames()) %>% mutate(colnum = 1:n()) %>% relocate(colnum)

df <- data_extract %>% select(doi, `HR`:pupil)
n_total <- df %>% pull(doi) %>% unique() %>% length()

# Step 1: Pivot to long format (no drop_na yet!)
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -doi, names_to = "measure", values_to = "transformation")

# Step 2: Calculate proportion of non-NA values BEFORE dropping NAs
measure_percent <- df_long %>%
  group_by(measure) %>%
  summarise(prop = mean(!is.na(transformation))) %>%
  mutate(measure_label = paste0(measure, " (", round(100 * prop, 1), "%)"))

# Step 3: Create label map
label_map <- setNames(measure_percent$measure_label, measure_percent$measure)

### change on label ""rc, sqrt (analysis 1); z (analysis 2)""
#df_long %>% filter(transformation %>% grepl(";", .)) #check columns with ";"
df_long <- df_long %>%
  # Separate on ";" into rows
  separate_rows(transformation, sep = ";") %>%
  # Remove the analysis part in parentheses
  mutate(transformation = str_trim(str_remove(transformation, "\\s*\\(.*?\\)")))

# Step 4: Now drop NAs and apply label map
df_long <- df_long %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(measure = label_map[measure])

counts <- df_long %>%
  count(measure, transformation, drop = F) #%>%
  #mutate(transformation = ifelse(is.na(transformation), "Missing", transformation))

df_wide <- counts %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(ID = paste0("T", row_number())) %>%
  relocate(ID)

id_labels <- df_wide %>% select(ID, transformation)
id_named_vec <- setNames(id_labels$transformation, id_labels$ID)

d <- df_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(ID, transformation), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Count") %>%
  filter(Count > 0) %>%
  mutate(Type = ifelse(Count > 1, "more than one study", "one study only"))

d <- setDT(d)

# Step: Create a unique transformation-to-ID mapping
id_order <- d[ , .SD[1], by = transformation][order(transformation)]$ID

# Apply it as the factor level order
d[, ID := factor(ID, levels = id_order)]
#d[, ID := factor(ID, levels = d[, .N, by = ID][order(N)]$ID)]
#d[, Measure := factor(Measure, levels = d[, .N, by = Measure][order(N)]$Measure)]
d[, Measure := factor(Measure, levels = sort(unique(Measure)))]
d[, Measure2 := as.numeric(Measure)]

# Modern, perceptually uniform color palette from scico
#pal1 <- scico(n = length(levels(d$Measure)), palette = "bilbao")
#pal1 <- scico::scico(n = length(levels(d$Measure)), palette = "batlow")
# pal1 <- scico::scico(n = length(levels(d$Measure)), palette = "berlin")
pal1 <- scico(n = length(levels(d$Measure)), palette = "roma")

ggplot(d, aes(x = ID, y = Measure2, color = Measure, shape = Type, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.8, color = "grey50") +   # softer connecting lines
  geom_point(size = 5, stroke = 1.2, fill = "white") +      # bigger points, white fill, clear outlines
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1:length(unique(d$Measure)), colour = "grey92", size = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1:length(unique(d$ID)), colour = "grey92", size = 0.3) +
  geom_rect(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 0.6, fill = "white", color = NA) +
  coord_polar() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(19, 21)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, length(unique(d$Measure)) + 1),
    breaks = 1:length(unique(d$Measure)),
    labels = levels(d$Measure)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal1) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = id_named_vec) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40"),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    #title = "Transformation Types by Measure and Study",
    #subtitle = paste0("Across ", n_total, " included studies"),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    shape = "Transformation count",
    color = paste0("Measure used in (% of ", n_total, " studies)")
  )

# Step 1: Calculate total counts per Measure
d[, total_measure_count := sum(Count), by = Measure]

# Step 2: Calculate percentage for each transformation within the measure
d[, pct := 100 * Count / total_measure_count]

# Step 3a: Create a label with percentage rounded, e.g. "45%"
d[, pct_label := paste0(round(pct, digits = 1), "%")]

pal1 <- pal_lipari(length(levels(d$Measure)))

# Step 3b: Renaming of cell entries
d$Measure <- gsub("eye", "EYE tracking", d$Measure)
d$Measure <- gsub("pupil", "PUPIL SIZE", d$Measure)
d$Measure <- gsub("startle", "EMG startle", d$Measure)

# Step 4: Add geom_text to the plot, adjust position with nudge_x or nudge_y
ggplot(d, aes(x = ID, y = Measure2, color = Measure, shape = Type, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.8, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = pct), stroke = 1.2, fill = "white") +  # SIZE mapped to pct
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1:length(unique(d$Measure)), colour = "grey92", size = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1:length(unique(d$ID)), colour = "grey92", size = 0.3) +
  geom_rect(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 0.6, fill = "white", color = NA) +
  coord_polar() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(19, 21)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, length(unique(d$Measure)) + 1),
    breaks = 1:length(unique(d$Measure)),
    labels = levels(d$Measure)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal1) +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 10), name = "Percentage within measure") +  # Dot size scale
  scale_x_discrete(labels = id_named_vec) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40"),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    shape = "Transformation count",
    color = paste0("Measure used in (% of ", n_total, " studies)")
  )

d_trans <- copy(d); id_named_vec_trans <- id_named_vec
```

```{r circle-plot-range-correction}
# Select columns
df <- data_extract %>% select(doi, `HR`:Range_correction_type, -dt_specs)
n_total <- df %>% pull(doi) %>% unique() %>% length()

# Step 1: Pivot to long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -doi, names_to = "measure", values_to = "transformation")

# Add range correction type
rc_info <- data_extract[ ,c("doi","Range_correction_type")]
df_long <- merge(df_long, rc_info, by = "doi", all.x = TRUE)
df_long$Range_correction_type[-grep("rc", df_long$transformation)] <- NA

# Step 2: Now drop NAs
df_long <- df_long %>%
  drop_na()

counts <- df_long %>%
  count(measure, Range_correction_type, drop = F) 

df_wide <- counts %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(ID = paste0("T", row_number())) %>%
  relocate(ID)

id_labels <- df_wide %>% select(ID, Range_correction_type)
id_named_vec <- setNames(id_labels$Range_correction_type, id_labels$ID)
id_named_vec <- gsub("_", " ", id_named_vec)

d <- df_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(ID, Range_correction_type), names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Count") %>%
  filter(Count > 0) %>%
  mutate(Type = ifelse(Count > 1, "more than one study", "one study only"))

d <- setDT(d)

# Step: Create a unique range-correction-type-to-ID mapping
id_order <- d[ , .SD[1], by = Range_correction_type][order(Range_correction_type)]$ID

# Apply it as the factor level order
d[, ID := factor(ID, levels = id_order)]
#d[, ID := factor(ID, levels = d[, .N, by = ID][order(N)]$ID)]
#d[, Measure := factor(Measure, levels = d[, .N, by = Measure][order(N)]$Measure)]
d[, Measure := factor(Measure, levels = sort(unique(Measure)))]
d[, Measure2 := as.numeric(Measure)]

### Calculate counts and percentages
# Step 1: Calculate total counts per Measure
d[, total_measure_count := sum(Count), by = Measure]

# Step 2: Calculate percentage for each transformation within the measure
d[, pct := 100 * Count / total_measure_count]

# Step 3: Create a label with percentage rounded, e.g. "45%"
d[, pct_label := paste0(round(pct, digits = 1), "%")]

# Step 4: Renaming of cell entries
d$Measure <- gsub("eye", "EYE tracking", d$Measure)
d$Measure <- gsub("pupil", "PUPIL SIZE", d$Measure)
d$Measure <- gsub("startle", "EMG startle", d$Measure)

### Color palette
d$Measure <- as.factor(d$Measure)
pal1 <- pal_lipari(length(levels(d$Measure)))

### PLOT
ggplot(d, aes(x = ID, y = Measure2, color = Measure, shape = Type, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.8, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(size = pct), stroke = 1.2, fill = "white") +  # SIZE mapped to pct
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1:length(unique(d$Measure)), colour = "grey92", size = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1:length(unique(d$ID)), colour = "grey92", size = 0.3) +
  geom_rect(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 0.6, fill = "white", color = NA) +
  coord_polar() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(19, 21)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, length(unique(d$Measure)) + 1),
    breaks = 1:length(unique(d$Measure)),
    labels = levels(d$Measure)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal1) +
  scale_size(range = c(2, 10), name = "Percentage within measure") +  # Dot size scale
  scale_x_discrete(labels = id_named_vec) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40"),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    shape = "Transformation count",
    color = paste0("Measure")
  )
```

```{r rc-stackedbar}
library(scico)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)

# Clean labels for the legend
d[, RC_label := gsub("_", " ", Range_correction_type)]
d[, RC_label := factor(RC_label, levels = unique(RC_label[order(ID)]))]

# Same palette family (lipari, reversed), now one color per correction type
pal_rc <- pal_lipari(nlevels(d$RC_label))

# NEW: number of studies before the percentage
# Name of the column in d that holds the number of studies.
# Leave as NULL to auto-detect from common names, or set it, e.g. "N_studies"
count_col <- NULL

if (is.null(count_col)) {
  candidates <- c("n_studies", "N_studies", "n", "N", "k", "K",
                  "count", "Count", "studies", "Studies", "n_papers", "N_papers")
  count_col <- intersect(candidates, names(d))[1]
}
if (is.na(count_col) || is.null(count_col)) {
  stop("No study-count column found. Columns in d are: ",
       paste(names(d), collapse = ", "),
       "\nSet count_col to the right one.")
}

# pct_label is your existing percentage label (e.g. "34%").
# This puts the count in front: "12 (34%)"
d[, pct_label := paste0(d[[count_col]], " (", round(pct), "%)")]

# Show a label only if the segment is big enough to be readable
d[, show_label := ifelse(pct >= 5, pct_label, "")]

ggplot(d, aes(x = Measure, y = pct, fill = RC_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = show_label),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3.8, color = "white", family = "Helvetica") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_rc, name = "Range correction type") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40"),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percentage within measure")

d_rc <- copy(d)
```

```{r merge-plots}
library(scico)

# ---- Panel A: circle plot of transformations ---------------------------------
d_trans[, Measure := factor(Measure, levels = sort(unique(as.character(Measure))))]
d_trans[, Measure2 := as.numeric(Measure)]
pal_A <- pal_lipari(nlevels(d_trans$Measure))

# ---- Panel A: circle plot of transformations ---------------------------------
pal_A <- pal_lipari(nlevels(d_trans$Measure))

p_A <- ggplot(d_trans, aes(x = ID, y = Measure2, color = Measure, shape = Type, group = ID)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey50") +

  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_A) +

  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    shape = "Transformation count",
    color = paste0("Measure used in (% of ", n_total, " studies)")
  )

# ---- Panel B: stacked bar of range correction types --------------------------
d_rc[, RC_label := gsub("_", " ", Range_correction_type)]
d_rc[, RC_label := factor(RC_label, levels = unique(RC_label[order(ID)]))]
pal_rc <- pal_lipari(nlevels(d_rc$RC_label))

# Label: studies in segment / total studies for the measure (percentage)
d_rc[, pct_label := paste0(Count, "/", total_measure_count, " (", round(pct), "%)")]
d_rc[, show_label := ifelse(pct >= 5, pct_label, "")]

p_B <- ggplot(d_rc, aes(x = Measure, y = pct, fill = RC_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = show_label),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3.8, color = "white", family = "Helvetica") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_rc, name = "Range correction type") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percentage within measure")

# ---- Combine -----------------------------------------------------------------
p_AB <- (p_A / p_B) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1.3, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20))

p_AB

# Save (adjust size as needed)
ggsave("Figure_AB.png", p_AB, width = 12, height = 18, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

```{r results-assumptions-overview}
# Select the data
data_assump <- data_extract %>%
  select(normality, homoscedasticity, sphericity, independence, linearity, multicollinearity)

names(data_assump) <- c("Normality","Homoscedasticity","Sphericity","Independence","Linearity","Multicollinearity")

# Reshape it from wide to long
data_assump <- data_assump %>%
  mutate(Sphericity = case_when(Sphericity == "not reported" ~ "not reported",
                                Sphericity %>% is.na() ~ NA, #TODO should this be mapped to "not reported"?
                                T ~ "yes")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Assumption", values_to = "Checked") %>%
  count(Assumption, Checked) %>%
  group_by(Assumption) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = n / sum(n),
    label = scales::percent(percent)
  )

# Factorize the assumptions and checked variable and reorder the levels (for a more intuitive order)
data_assump$Assumption <- as.factor(data_assump$Assumption)
data_assump$Assumption <- factor(data_assump$Assumption, 
                                  levels = c("Normality","Homoscedasticity","Sphericity",
                                             "Independence","Linearity","Multicollinearity"))

data_assump$Checked <- as.factor(data_assump$Checked)
data_assump$Checked <- factor(data_assump$Checked, 
                                  levels = c("not reported","not specified","yes",
                                             "dependent variable"))

ggplot(data_assump, aes(x = factor(Assumption), y = n, fill = Checked)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_lipari(n_lev(data_assump$Checked))) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), 
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), 
            color = "white", size = 3.8) +
  labs(y = "Number of studies", fill = "Checked") +
  lit_theme +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top")+
  coord_flip()   
```

```{r assumptions-pie-charts}
df_cake$normality[df_cake$normality != "not reported"] <- "yes"

# Set names for plot titles
names(df_cake) <- c("Normality","Homoscedasticity","Sphericity","Linearity","Multicollinearity")

# Prepare the plot data frame
df_long <- df_cake %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "assumption", values_to = "status") %>%
  group_by(assumption, status) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(assumption) %>%
  mutate(
    percent = count / sum(count),
    label = paste0(round(percent * 100, digits = 1), "% (", count, ")"),
    ymax = cumsum(percent),
    ymin = lag(ymax, default = 0),
    label_pos = (ymin + ymax) / 2
  )

# Function to create pie chart with outer label positions
create_pie <- function(var_name) {
  df_sub <- df_long %>% filter(assumption == var_name)
  
  ggplot(df_sub, aes(ymax = ymax, ymin = ymin, xmax = 1, xmin = 0, fill = status)) +
    geom_rect(color = "white") +
    geom_text(
      aes(x = 1.2, y = label_pos, label = label),
      size = 3.8, color = "black"
    ) +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    xlim(c(-0.5, 1.5)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_lipari(n_lev(df_sub$status))) +
    theme_void(base_size = 14, base_family = lit_font) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    labs(fill = "Status",
      title = var_name
    )
}

# Collect pies
pies <- unique(df_long$assumption) %>% map(create_pie)
```

### c. Transformation Practices

specification of data transformation method, rationale, was the transformation applied on trial or average level

the different data transformations (how many studies use raw data?)

```{r new-sankeyloop}
# Function 
make_sankey2 <- function(label, transf_col, rationale_col = 49, data = data_extract) {
  d <- na.omit(data[, c(transf_col, rationale_col)])
  names(d) <- c("transf", "rationale_di")
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    message("Skipping ", label, ": no complete rows after na.omit()")
    return(NULL)
  }
  d_long <- make_long(d, transf, rationale_di)

  ggplot(d_long, aes(x = x, next_x = next_x,
                     node = node, next_node = next_node,
                     label = factor(node))) +
    geom_sankey(flow.alpha = 0.7, aes(fill = factor(node))) +
    geom_sankey_label(size = 3.8, color = 1, fill = "white", family = lit_font) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_lipari(n_lev(d_long$node))) +
    scale_x_discrete(breaks = c("transf", "rationale_di"),
                     labels = c("Transformation", "Rationale")) +
    ggtitle(paste0(label, ": Data transformation methods and reporting rationale")) +
    lit_theme +
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}

#create df
# (labels follow the naming used in the circle plot of transformations)
measures <- data.frame(
  label      = c("SCR", "SCL", "EMG startle", "HR", "HRV", "EYE tracking", "PUPIL SIZE"),
  file       = c("scr", "scl", "emgstartle", "hr", "hrv", "eyetrack", "pupil"),
  transf_col = c(43,     44,    42,            39,         40,    45,             46),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

#run loop with saving on
save_plots <- TRUE   # set FALSE to only display

sankey_plots <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(measures))) {
  m <- measures[i, ]
  p <- tryCatch(
    make_sankey2(m$label, m$transf_col),
    error = function(e) { message("Failed for ", m$label, ": ", e$message); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(p)) next
  sankey_plots[[m$file]] <- p
  print(p)
  if (save_plots) {
    ggsave(paste0("datatransf_rationale_", m$file, "_sankey.png"),
           plot = p, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

```{r results-outlier}
### Outlier removal methods
#data.frame(colname = data_extract %>% colnames()) %>% mutate(colnum = 1:n()) %>% relocate(colnum)
data_outlier <- data_extract %>%
  select(outlier, outlier_when, outlier_how) %>% 
  rename_with(~ c("outlier_reported", "outlier_scope", "outlier_criterion"), everything()) %>%  
  filter(!if_all(everything(), ~ is.na(.) | . == ""))

# previous code scrap: check why this row was changed
# mutate(
#     outlier_scope = ifelse(row_number() == 34, "not reported", outlier_scope))  

# Group outlier categories 
data_outlier_grouped <- data_outlier %>%
  mutate(
    outlier_criterion_group = case_when(
      str_detect(outlier_criterion, regex("\\bSD\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "SD-based threshold (e.g., ± 3 SD)",
      str_detect(outlier_criterion, regex("\\bZ\\b")) ~ "Z-based threshold (e.g., Z > 3)",
      str_detect(outlier_criterion, regex("IQR", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "IQR-based threshold (e.g., > Q3 + 1.5*IQR)",
      str_detect(outlier_criterion, regex("Mahalanobis|Grubbs|correlation", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "statistical tests (e.g., Mahalanobis distance, Smirmov–Grubbs)",
      str_detect(outlier_criterion, "visual inspection") ~ "manual visual inspection",
      str_detect(outlier_criterion, regex("not reported", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "not reported",
      is.na(outlier_criterion) ~ NA_character_,
      TRUE ~ "other"
    )
  )

# Convert to long format
data_outlier_grouped_long <- data_outlier_grouped%>%
  make_long(outlier_reported, outlier_scope, outlier_criterion_group) %>%
  filter(!if_all(c(node), is.na))

### Outlier removal: Sankey Plot 
ggplot(data_outlier_grouped_long, 
       aes(x = x,
           next_x = next_x,
           node = node,
           next_node = next_node,
           fill = factor(node),
           label = node)) +
  geom_sankey(flow.alpha = 0.5, node.color = 1) +
  geom_sankey_label(size = 3.8, color = 1, fill = "white", family = lit_font) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_lipari(n_lev(data_outlier_grouped_long$node))) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = c("outlier_reported", "outlier_scope", "outlier_criterion_group"),
                   labels = c("Outlier removal reported?", "Scope", "Criterion")) +
  ggtitle("Outlier removal: reporting practices, scope and outlier criterion") +
  lit_theme + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

#ggsave("outlier_removal_sankey.png", width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)

# Group the outlier criterion thresholds by type (SD-, IQR- or Z-based)
data_outlier_grouped_plots <- data_outlier_grouped %>%
  mutate(
    cutoff_value = case_when(
      outlier_criterion_group == "IQR-based threshold (e.g., > Q3 + 1.5*IQR)" ~ str_extract(outlier_criterion, "\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(?=\\*IQR)"),
      outlier_criterion_group %in% c("SD-based threshold (e.g., ± 3 SD)", "Z-based threshold (e.g., Z > 3)") ~ str_extract(outlier_criterion, "\\d+(\\.\\d+)?"),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    cutoff_value = as.numeric(cutoff_value)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(cutoff_value))  # Keep only valid cutoffs

### Barplot of individual outlier criterion thresholds
ggplot(data_outlier_grouped_plots, aes(x = factor(cutoff_value), fill = outlier_criterion_group)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack") +
  labs(
    title = "Most common outlier thresholds by criterion type",
    x = "Threshold value", y = "Number of studies", fill = "Criterion group") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_lipari(n_lev(data_outlier_grouped_plots$outlier_criterion_group))) +
  lit_theme + 
  theme(legend.position = "right")

#ggsave("outlier_removal_thresholds_barplot.png", width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

```{r stackedbar-openVariables}
dat <- as.data.table(data_extract)   # <- your study-level data (one row per study)

vars <- c("open_data", "open_code", "open_material", "prereg")

# ---- Long format -------------------------------------------------------------
long <- melt(dat, measure.vars = vars,
             variable.name = "Measure", value.name = "status")

# Harmonise coding: yes/no style values, missing shown as its own category
long[, status := tolower(trimws(as.character(status)))]
long[status %in% c("true", "1", "y", "yes"),  status := "yes"]
long[status %in% c("false", "0", "n", "no"),  status := "no"]
long[is.na(status) | status == "" | status == "na", status := "not reported"]

# Category order (adds any extra categories found in the data)
lev <- unique(c("yes", "no", "not reported", sort(unique(long$status))))
long[, status_label := factor(status, levels = lev[lev %in% status])]

# Clean x-axis labels
long[, Measure := factor(Measure, levels = vars,
                         labels = c("Open data", "Open code",
                                    "Open material", "Preregistration"))]

# ---- Counts and percentages within each measure ------------------------------
d <- long[, .N, by = .(Measure, status_label)]
d[, pct := 100 * N / sum(N), by = Measure]
d[, pct_label := paste0(N, " (", round(pct), "%)")]
d[, show_label := ifelse(pct >= 5, pct_label, "")]

# ---- Palette (lipari, one colour per category) -------------------------------
pal_st <- scico(nlevels(d$status_label), palette = "lipari", begin = 0.1, end = 0.85)
# If you already have pal_lipari() defined, use: pal_st <- pal_lipari(nlevels(d$status_label))

# ---- Plot --------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(d, aes(x = Measure, y = pct, fill = status_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = show_label),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = 3.8, color = "white", family = "Helvetica") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_st, name = "Status") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey40"),
    panel.border = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Percentage of studies")

d_open <- copy(d)


# Text for manuscript: 
n_total <- d_open[Measure == "Open data", sum(N)]

# Returns "n (xx%)" for a given measure and status
fmt <- function(measure, status = "yes") {
  r <- d_open[Measure == measure & status_label == status]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) return("0 (0%)")
  sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", r$N, r$pct)
}

# Returns only the percentage, e.g. "34%"
pc <- function(measure, status = "yes") {
  r <- d_open[Measure == measure & status_label == status]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) return("0%")
  sprintf("%.0f%%", r$pct)
}

library(data.table)

# ---- Print the numbers in the console ----------------------------------------
cat("\nOpen-science practices (N =", n_total, "studies)\n")
cat(strrep("-", 50), "\n")

# Full table: counts and percentages per measure and status
print(
  dcast(d_open, Measure ~ status_label, value.var = "N", fill = 0L)
)

# One line per practice
for (m in levels(d_open$Measure)) {
  cat(sprintf("%-16s yes: %s | no: %s | not reported: %s\n",
              m, fmt(m, "yes"), fmt(m, "no"), fmt(m, "not reported")))
}

#Print the Results sentence as plain text 
txt <- sprintf(
  paste0("Open-science practices were uncommon across the %d included studies ",
         "(Supplementary Fig. X). Preregistration was reported in %s of studies, ",
         "and materials were shared in %s. Data were openly available in %s of ",
         "studies, whereas analysis code was shared in only %s. For %s of studies, ",
         "code availability was not reported at all."),
  n_total,
  fmt("Preregistration"), fmt("Open material"),
  fmt("Open data"), fmt("Open code"),
  fmt("Open code", "no")
)

cat("\n", strwrap(txt, width = 80), sep = "\n")
```

### Open-science practices

Open-science practices were uncommon across the `r n_total` included studies
(Supplementary Fig. X). Preregistration was reported in `r fmt("Preregistration")`
of studies, and materials were shared in `r fmt("Open material")`. Data were
openly available in `r fmt("Open data")` of studies, whereas analysis code was
shared in only `r fmt("Open code")`. For `r fmt("Open code", "not reported")`
of studies, code availability was not reported at all. Sharing was thus most
frequent for materials and least frequent for analysis code, the resource most
needed to reproduce the transformation and scoring pipelines described above.

```{r sample-retensions}
dat <- as.data.table(data_extract)
study_col <- "doi"   # <- column that identifies the study (e.g. "ID", "study", "citation")

phys <- c("HR", "HRV", "orbicularis_oculi", "startle", "SCR", "SCL", "eye", "pupil")
phys <- phys[phys %in% names(dat)]

# ---- Parse n_after_exclusion -------------------------------------------------
# "SCR: 100; startle: 94"  -> one value per named measure
# "88"                     -> assigned to the physio column(s) that are not NA
parse_row <- function(i) {
  x <- as.character(dat$n_after_exclusion[i])
  if (is.na(x) || trimws(x) == "") return(NULL)

  # physio measures recorded in this study (anything other than NA / empty)
  used <- phys[vapply(phys, function(p) {
    v <- dat[[p]][i]
    !is.na(v) && trimws(as.character(v)) != ""
  }, logical(1))]

  if (grepl(":", x)) {
    parts <- trimws(strsplit(x, ";")[[1]])
    parts <- parts[grepl(":", parts)]
    nm  <- trimws(sub(":.*$", "", parts))
    val <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", sub("^.*:", "", parts)))
    key <- phys[match(tolower(gsub(" ", "_", nm)), tolower(phys))]
    if (anyNA(key))
      warning("Row ", i, ": unmatched measure name(s): ",
              paste(nm[is.na(key)], collapse = ", "))
    out <- data.table(row_id = i, physio = key, n_after = val, ambiguous = FALSE)
    return(out[!is.na(physio)])
  }

  val <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", x))
  if (length(used) == 0) {
    warning("Row ", i, ": single number but no physio column filled; skipped.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  data.table(row_id = i, physio = used, n_after = val,
             ambiguous = length(used) > 1)
}

after <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(dat)), parse_row))

# ---- Combine with n_before_exclusion ----------------------------------------
base <- dat[, .(row_id = .I,
                study = as.character(get(study_col)),
                n_before = as.numeric(n_before_exclusion))]
d_ret <- merge(after, base, by = "row_id")

# Single number that applies to several physio measures -> check manually
if (any(d_ret$ambiguous)) {
  message("Single N applied to several physio measures in these studies (check!):")
  print(unique(d_ret[ambiguous == TRUE, .(study, physio, n_after)]))
}

if (any(d_ret$n_after > d_ret$n_before, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  warning("n_after > n_before in some rows; excluded set to 0 there.")
}

d_ret[, excluded := pmax(n_before - n_after, 0)]

# Long format for stacking 
long <- melt(d_ret, id.vars = c("study", "physio", "n_before"),
             measure.vars = c("n_after", "excluded"),
             variable.name = "part", value.name = "n")
long[, part := factor(part, levels = c("excluded", "n_after"),
                      labels = c("Excluded", "Retained"))]   # Retained = left, Excluded = right

# Sort studies by n_before within each panel (free_y drops unused levels)
ord <- unique(long[, .(study, n_before)])[order(n_before)]
long[, study := factor(study, levels = unique(ord$study))]
long[, physio := factor(physio, levels = phys[phys %in% unique(physio)])]

library(patchwork)

# ---- Naming and colours as in the circle plots --------------------------------
phys_present <- sort(levels(long$physio))            # same alphabetical order as Measure levels
pal_meas <- setNames(pal_lipari(length(phys_present)), phys_present)

label_measure <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("eye",     "EYE tracking", x)
  x <- gsub("pupil",   "PUPIL SIZE",   x)
  x <- gsub("startle", "EMG startle",  x)
  gsub("_", " ", x)
}

col_excluded <- "#D1352B"

# ---- Plot ---------------------------------------------------------------------
big   <- intersect(c("SCR", "startle"), phys_present)
small <- setdiff(phys_present, big)

make_panel <- function(p) {
  ggplot(long[physio == p], aes(x = n, y = study, fill = part)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.8, color = NA) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Retained = unname(pal_meas[p]),
                                 Excluded = col_excluded),
                      drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14, base_family = "Helvetica") +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0),
      panel.border = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(title = label_measure(p), x = "Number of participants", y = "Studies")
}

panels <- setNames(lapply(c(big, small), make_panel), c(big, small))

top    <- wrap_plots(panels[big],   ncol = length(big))
bottom <- wrap_plots(panels[small], ncol = 3)

p_ret <- top / bottom + plot_layout(heights = c(2, 1))
p_ret

```
